correctness.rationale: For any specified adjacent pair, it occurs with probability 1/(2n-1), and deleting that pair conditionally leaves a uniform matching on 2n-2 positions without altering crossings. Summing over all 2n cyclic adjacent pairs proves the Palm identity, including point mass tests. Unconditional deletion of the chord incident to a distinguished endpoint couples X_(n-1)<=X_n. Counting disjoint adjacent pairs gives E[S_n(S_n-1)]=2n/(2n-1) for n>=2 and variance 4n(n-1)/(2n-1)^2. Crossings have established E X_n=n(n-1)/6 and variance n(n-1)(n+3)/45; correlation follows algebraically. Independent exhaustive matching enumeration n=2,3,4,5 verifies the Palm identity at every crossing atom, the means, variances and exact covariance/correlation; not an all-n proof.

value.rationale: Simple chords are a natural local isolation statistic and crossings a natural global intersection statistic in the same uniformly random matching. The exact all-test-function Palm identity, monotone negative regression and sharp finite-n correlation explain an otherwise nontrivial local/global dependence and can be reused for nonlinear crossing functionals, beyond two marginal approximations.
